cards.front: Recall a key point about Economic Geology & Resources
cards.back: An ore is a naturally occurring mineral from which a metal can be economically extracted

cards.front: Recall a key point about Economic Geology & Resources
cards.back: Hydrothermal ore deposits: metal-rich hot fluids deposit minerals in veins and fractures (e.g. tin in Cornwall, gold veins)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Economic Geology & Resources
cards.back: Placer deposits: heavy minerals concentrated by river or wave action (e.g. gold, diamond placers)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Economic Geology & Resources
cards.back: Fossil fuels: coal (from Carboniferous swamp forests), petroleum (from marine microorganisms under heat and pressure)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Economic Geology & Resources
cards.back: Evaporite deposits: salt, gypsum and potash formed by evaporation of restricted seawater bodies

cards.front: Recall a key point about Economic Geology & Resources
cards.back: Groundwater is stored in aquifers (porous, permeable rocks like sandstone and limestone); it is a vital resource

cards.front: What should you know about gcse geology exam tips — economic geology & resources?
cards.back: 1. For Economic Geology & Resources questions, use correct geological terminology and classify features precisely 2. Reference specific geological time periods and processes 3. When interpreting data, consider the quality and limitations of the evidence 4. Apply your understanding of Economic Geology & Resources to fieldwork observations and map data 5. For evaluation, weigh competing geological theories with evidence
